about: Relations: each later record in the findings ledger that treats a published finding, with the standing word read from the ledger line (DATA.md: held for a recheck that reproduced, narrowed for a scope cut, extended for later work built on it, questioned for a doubt not yet settled). A finding that is only listed under another entry's 'Relates to' line, with no treatment stated, gets no relation. Standing is derived from these at build time, never stored on a finding. Redirects: a refuted or retracted finding's page redirects to the finding that replaced it (null sends it to its entry on the findings index); the build fails when a refuted or retracted finding has no entry here.

relations.note: A repeat of test A on gridded scPDSI near each site gave +0.025, below the time-shift 95th percentile of 0.038; the kill fires again.
The +0.037 sign under division PDSI with species effects does not survive site-scale drought.
Adds the cost term the rod lacked; removing it reproduces F63 B3 and B4.
Constant-rate copying follows F63's 1/(n+1) form at r 0.993.

relations.scope: film fit and its planted recovery
relations.note: The film fit passed log10 sigma into a model of log10 variance. On true variance the errors are 0.186 and 0.068; the failed verdict stands and the pattern of hit numbers changes.

relations.scope: film hinge within the sheet's range
relations.note: The hinge sits within the sheet's range, as F147 said, now on BIC.

relations.scope: size of the ratios and the gain from combining observers
relations.note: Under photon noise the set 1 ratios fall to 1.67 for the bee and 1.50 for the blue tit, and the gain from combining two observers, +0.39 and found after the fact, shrinks to a null. Publication carries the direction only.
relations.source: findings ledger, F88 and Publication pass corrections 2026-11-09

relations.note: On 161 held-out boreal sites the panel instrument's kill fired too; F132's block on direction readings stands.

relations.scope: account of the planted lag-1 arm
relations.note: Exploratory and post hoc: a negative prior-summer term adds to the Granger signal, so F132's absorption account holds only for same-sign terms, and its planted arm had the wrong sign for these stands.

relations.scope: direction on rings, read on a panel
relations.note: A third round on 145 new sites: the lagged panel instrument passes every binding verdict but one and earns exclusion and forward status at that coupling strength.
On a third held-out panel the negative prior-summer term is species-dependent, not a panel result; the same instrument passes every binding verdict but one there.
F152's corpus gap ranking stays failed.
Newton's thick-plate rings run about 0.8 percent large; with F14, both experiments suggest his 1/89000 inch is 2 to 3 percent thick.
Newton's colour limits read as half-wavelengths: the same interval sits 3 percent short against a different reference, so the sign is not a contradiction.
A single split of noise and field bias ranks failed replications on the same RPP and FReD set (Brier 0.222 against 0.256), adding nothing to the z value alone.
On 649 development series no drift-aware option beat the original bound (rho 0.350 to 0.398 against 0.414); same data family, not independent.
The two-lines test rejects a U for calm against arousal: the quadratic term is significant (p 0.012) and the relation is a fall that levels off.
A later review of our ledger recorded one error: the rerun bound is far below the published limit, so the headline was narrowed to a reproduction of method.
A later review of our ledger recorded an error and a control that could not fail: the sampling changed after the search route refused, and fitted lines pass by construction.
A later review of our ledger recorded one value entered from memory: the three forms were written from memory, so the result covers these three versions only.
A later review of our ledger recorded a failed planted check and an error: the first planted check failed, and the entry was self-graded and not blind, with order confounded with condition.

A later review of our ledger recorded a failed planted check, an error and an explanation added after the result; on 2026-11-09 the ledger added that the preregistered reproduction check failed at 0.287 against 0.234 within 0.03.
relations.source: findings ledger, F422 correction pass and Publication pass corrections 2026-11-09

relations.note: A later review of our ledger recorded one error: the public 10 percent sample has low power, so the claim covers large patterns only.

relations.scope: reused inputs and a proxy truth
relations.note: A later review of our ledger recorded two errors: later tables reuse inputs, and the Hubble constant truth is a proxy.

corrections_about: Dated corrections in the findings ledger that the paper's own Corrections section does not carry. The record builder adds them to the finding's trail beside the paper's.

corrections.reason: The ledger entry read Merkle and colleagues (2017) as finding the opposite sign: good forecasters select more questions.
corrections.after: The abstract we read does not state that sign, so the reading is unconfirmed until the full paper is read. The paper and this page say so.
